units.zh: 劉鄩，密州安丘縣人也。
units.en: Liu Xun came from Anqiu in Mizhou.
units.literal: Liu Xun, a man of Anqiu county in Mizhou.

units.zh: 祖綬，密州戶掾，累贈左散騎常侍。
units.en: His grandfather Shou had served as Mizhou household recorder and was posthumously made Left Regular Cavalry Attendant.
units.literal: His grandfather Shou was household recorder of Mizhou, posthumously advanced repeatedly to Left Regular Cavalry Attendant.

units.zh: 父融，安丘令，累贈工部尚書。
units.en: His father Rong had been magistrate of Anqiu and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
units.literal: His father Rong was magistrate of Anqiu, posthumously advanced repeatedly to Minister of Works.

units.zh: 鄩幼有大志，好兵略，涉獵史傳。
units.en: As a youth he aimed high, studied warfare, and read widely in history.
units.literal: From youth Xun had great ambition, loved military strategy, and ranged through historical writings.

units.zh: 唐中和中，事青州節度使王敬武為小校。
units.en: During Tang Zhonghe he was a staff officer under Qingzhou commissioner Wang Jingwu.
units.literal: In the Zhonghe era of Tang he served Qingzhou military commissioner Wang Jingwu as a junior officer.

units.zh: 敬武卒，三軍推其子師範為留後，朝廷命崔安潛鎮青州，州人拒命。
units.en: After Jingwu's death the army made Shifan acting commissioner; the court sent Cui Anqian to Qingzhou, but the province would not obey.
units.literal: When Jingwu died the three armies pushed his son Shifan as acting commissioner; the court appointed Cui Anqian to govern Qingzhou, and the province refused the order.

units.zh: 棣州刺史張蟾將襲師範，師範遣都指揮使盧宏攻棣州，宏反與蟾通，偽旋軍以襲師範。
units.en: Dizhou prefect Zhang Chan planned to attack Shifan; Shifan sent overall commander Lu Hong against Dizhou, but Hong colluded with Chan and pretended to march home in order to surprise Shifan.
units.literal: Dizhou prefect Zhang Chan was about to strike Shifan; Shifan sent overall commander Lu Hong to attack Dizhou; Hong turned traitor, joined Chan, and feigned withdrawal to ambush Shifan.

units.zh: 師範知之，設伏兵以迎宏，既而享之，先誡鄩曰：「宏至即斬之。」
units.en: Shifan learned of the plot, laid an ambush for Hong, then feasted him and told Xun beforehand, "The moment Hong arrives, kill him."
units.literal: Shifan learned of it, set ambush troops to receive Hong, and afterward entertained him, first warning Xun: "When Hong arrives, cut off his head at once."

units.zh: 鄩如約，斬弧於座上，同亂者皆誅之。
units.en: Xun did as ordered, slew Hong in his seat, and put every conspirator to death.
units.literal: Xun kept his word, beheaded Hong at table, and all who shared in the mutiny were executed.

units.zh: 師範以鄩為馬步軍副都指揮使，攻下棣州，殺張蟾，朝廷因授師範平盧軍節度使。
units.en: Shifan named Xun deputy commander of horse and foot, captured Dizhou, killed Zhang Chan, and the court then gave Shifan the Pinglu commission.
units.literal: Shifan made Xun deputy overall commander of horse and foot, took Dizhou, killed Zhang Chan, and the court thereupon appointed Shifan military commissioner of the Pinglu army.

units.zh: 光化初，師範表鄩為登州刺史。
units.en: Early in Guanghua Shifan recommended Xun for Deng prefecture.
units.literal: At the start of Guanghua, Shifan memorialized Xun as prefect of Deng.

units.zh: 歲餘，移刺淄州，署行軍司馬。
units.en: A year later he was transferred to Zi and made acting chief of staff.
units.literal: After more than a year he was moved to govern Zi prefecture and was appointed acting chief of staff.

units.zh: 天復元年，昭宗幸鳳翔，太祖率四鎮之師奉迎於岐下。
units.en: In Tianfu 1 Zhaozong went to Fengxiang; the Founder marched the four circuits to Qi to bring him back.
units.literal: Tianfu year 1, Emperor Zhaozong went to Fengxiang; the Founder led troops of the four circuits to welcome him below Qi.

units.zh: 李茂貞與內官韓全誨矯詔征天下兵入援，師範覽詔，慷慨泣下，遣心腹乘虛襲取太祖管內州郡。
units.en: Li Maozhen and eunuch Han Quanhui forged an edict calling up armies everywhere; Shifan wept when he read it and sent trusted agents to raid the Founder's holdings.
units.literal: Li Maozhen and the inner attendant Han Quanhui forged an edict to summon troops empire-wide; Shifan read it, wept in passion, and sent trusted men to seize by surprise the Founder's prefectures and counties.

units.zh: 所在同日竊發，其事多泄，唯鄩以偏師陷兗州，遂據其郡。
units.en: Revolts broke out the same day across the region; most were betrayed, but Xun with a flank force seized Yanzhou and held it.
units.literal: Everywhere rose on the same day; most plots leaked, but Xun alone with a detached column took Yanzhou and held the commandery.

units.zh: 初，鄩遣細人詐為鬻油者，覘兗城內虛實及出入之所，視羅城下一水竇可以引眾而入，遂誌之。
units.en: He had sent spies disguised as oil peddlers to learn Yan's defenses and found a drain under the outer wall wide enough for men; he noted it for the assault.
units.literal: Earlier Xun had sent agents posing as oil sellers to spy out Yan's strength and the routes in and out; he saw a water opening under the outer wall through which troops could enter, and marked it.

units.zh: 鄩乃告師範，請步兵五百，宵自水竇銜枚而入，一夕而定，軍城晏然，市民無擾。
units.en: He asked Shifan for five hundred infantry, slipped in by night through the drain with gags, and took the inner city in a single night without alarming the populace.
units.literal: Xun then told Shifan, asked for five hundred foot soldiers, and at night entered through the drain with gags in their mouths; in one night the city was settled, the garrison calm, and the townspeople undisturbed.

units.zh: 〈（《金華子》云：鄩入據子城，甲兵精銳，城內人皆束手，莫敢旅拒。
units.en: (The 《Jinhua Zi》 records that once Xun held the inner citadel his troops were elite and the townspeople dared not resist.
units.literal: (The 《Jinhua Zi》 says: When Xun entered and held the inner city, his armor was sharp; everyone in the city was helpless and none dared resist in a body.

units.zh: 加以州將悍，人情不附，鄩因而撫治，民皆安堵。）〉
units.en: The prefect was brutal and unpopular; Xun won the people over and restored order.)〉
units.literal: Moreover the prefect was fierce and the people were not attached to him; Xun therefore pacified and governed them, and all households were secure.)〉

units.zh: 太祖命大將葛從周攻之。
units.en: The Founder sent Ge Congzhou against him.
units.literal: The Founder ordered the great general Ge Congzhou to attack him.

units.zh: 時從周為節度使，領兵在外，州城為鄩所據，家屬悉在城中。
units.en: Congzhou was commissioner in the field while Xun held the city and his entire household was within.
units.literal: At that time Congzhou was military commissioner and led troops abroad; the prefectural city was held by Xun and all his family were inside.

units.zh: 鄩善撫其家，移就外第，供給有禮，升堂拜從周之母。
units.en: Xun cared for the family, lodged them outside the walls, provided for them generously, and paid his respects to Congzhou's mother.
units.literal: Xun treated the family well, moved them to an outer residence, supplied them courteously, and went up to the hall to bow to Congzhou's mother.

units.zh: 及從周攻城，鄩以板輿請母登城，母告從周曰：「劉將軍待我甚至，不異於兒，新婦已下，並不失所。
units.en: During the siege Xun brought the mother to the ramparts in a litter; she called to Congzhou, "General Liu has been as kind to me as a son, and your wife and household have been well provided for.
units.literal: When Congzhou besieged the city, Xun had a litter bring the mother to the wall; she told Congzhou: "General Liu has treated me extremely well, no less than a son; my daughter-in-law and all below her have lacked for nothing.

units.zh: 劉將軍與爾各為其主，爾其察之。」
units.en: He and you serve different masters—consider that carefully."
units.literal: General Liu and you each serve his own lord—consider that carefully."

units.zh: 從周歔欷而退。
units.en: Congzhou wept and withdrew.
units.literal: Congzhou sighed and withdrew.

units.zh: 鄩料簡城中老疾及婦人浮食百姓不足與守者，悉出之於外，與將士同甘苦，分衣食，以抗外軍，戢兵禁暴，居人泰然。
units.en: He expelled the old, sick, women, and useless mouths from the city, shared rations with his men, disciplined the garrison, and kept the people calm under siege.
units.literal: Xun sorted out the aged, sick, women, and townspeople with only floating rations who were unfit to hold the walls and sent them all outside, sharing hardship with the soldiers, dividing food and clothing to resist the besiegers, restraining troops and forbidding violence, so the residents were at ease.

units.zh: 從周攻圍既久，鄩無外援，人情稍有去就之意。
units.en: The siege wore on without relief, and morale inside Yan began to crack.
units.literal: Congzhou's siege dragged on; Xun had no outside relief, and minds in the city began to waver.

units.zh: 一日，節度副使王彥溫逾城而奔，守陴者從之而逸，鄩之守兵禁之不可，鄩即遣人從容告彥溫曰：「請副使少將人出，非素遣者請勿帶行。」
units.en: Deputy commissioner Wang Yanwen fled over the wall and others followed; Xun could not hold them back and sent word, "Take only the men I authorized—no one else."
units.literal: One day deputy commissioner Wang Yanwen climbed the wall and fled; wall guards followed him out; Xun's troops could not stop them; Xun at once sent someone calmly to tell Yanwen: "Ask the deputy to take only a few men out; those not previously sent, please do not take along."

units.zh: 又揚言於眾曰：「素遣從副使行者即勿禁，其擅去者族之。」
units.en: He announced to the crowd, "Those who leave on the deputy's prior orders are not to be stopped; whoever goes on his own, his clan will be destroyed."
units.literal: He also proclaimed to the crowd: "Those who leave on the deputy's prior orders are not to be stopped; whoever goes on his own, his clan will be destroyed."

units.zh: 守民聞之皆感，奔逸者乃止。
units.en: The garrison was heartened and the flight ended.
units.literal: Hearing it, the defenders were moved, and those who had fled then stopped.

units.zh: 外軍聞之，果疑彥溫有奸，即戮之於城下，自是軍城遂固。
units.en: The besiegers suspected Yanwen of collusion and killed him before the walls; after that the defense stiffened.
units.literal: The besiegers heard it and indeed suspected Yanwen of treachery; they at once executed him below the wall; from then on the city held firm.

units.zh: 及王師範兵力漸窘，從周以禍福諭鄩，俾之革麵，鄩報曰：「俟青州本使歸降，即以城池還納。」
units.en: As Shifan weakened, Congzhou appealed to Xun to surrender; Xun replied, "Wait until the Qingzhou commissioner himself submits, and I will return the city."
units.literal: When Shifan's strength grew tight, Congzhou urged fortune and misfortune on Xun and bade him change sides; Xun replied: "Wait until the Qingzhou commissioner himself submits, and I will return the city."

units.zh: 天復三年十一月，師範告降，且言先差行軍司馬劉鄩領兵入兗州，請釋其罪，亦以告鄩，鄩即出城聽命。
units.en: In the eleventh month of Tianfu 3 Shifan surrendered, named Xun's occupation of Yan, and asked pardon; Xun then marched out and submitted.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of Tianfu year 3 Shifan announced surrender, saying he had first sent chief of staff Liu Xun with troops into Yanzhou and asking that his crime be forgiven; he also informed Xun, and Xun at once left the city to await orders.

units.zh: 太祖嘉其節概，以為有李英公之風。
units.en: The Founder admired his conduct and compared him to Li Jing.
units.literal: The Founder praised his integrity and said he had the manner of Lord Li of Ying.

units.zh: 鄩既降，從周具行裝服馬，請鄩歸大梁。
units.en: Congzhou fitted him with mounts and fine clothes for the journey to Daliang.
units.literal: After Xun submitted, Congzhou prepared traveling gear, horses, and dress and asked Xun to return to Daliang.

units.zh: 鄩曰：「未受梁王舍釋之旨，乘肥衣裘，非敢聞命。」
units.en: Xun refused: "Without the Prince of Liang's pardon I will not ride in splendor."
units.literal: Xun said: "I have not yet received the Liang prince's order of release; to ride fat horses in fur coats—I dare not obey."

units.zh: 即素服跨驢而發。
units.en: He set out in hemp robes on a mule.
units.literal: He went off in plain dress on a donkey.

units.zh: 及將謁見，太祖令賜冠帶，鄩曰：「累囚負罪，請就縶而入。」
units.en: Before audience the Founder offered him regalia; Xun said, "I am a repeated prisoner bearing guilt—I ask to enter in bonds."
units.literal: When he was about to have audience, the Founder ordered a cap and belt bestowed; Xun said: "A repeated prisoner bearing guilt—I ask to enter in bonds."

units.zh: 太祖不許。
units.en: The Founder refused.
units.literal: The Founder would not allow it.

units.zh: 及見，慰撫移時，且飲之酒，鄩以量小告太祖。
units.en: The Founder received him kindly and poured wine; Xun pleaded that he could not drink much.
units.literal: At the meeting he comforted him for some time and offered wine; Xun said his capacity was small and told the Founder so.

units.zh: 太祖曰：「取兗州，量何大耶！」
units.en: The Founder said, "Your capacity for taking Yanzhou was rather large!"
units.literal: The Founder said: "When you took Yanzhou, how great was your capacity!"

units.zh: 旋授元從都押牙。
units.en: He was soon made chief yamen officer of the Founder's personal following.
units.literal: He was soon appointed chief jailer of the Founder's personal following.

units.zh: 太祖牙下諸將，皆四鎮舊人，鄩一旦以羈旅之臣，驟居眾人之右，及與諸將相見，並用階庭之禮，太祖尤奇重之。
units.en: The Founder's generals were veterans of the four circuits; Xun, a newcomer, suddenly outranked them yet greeted each with full courtesy, and the Founder valued him all the more.
units.literal: All the generals under the Founder were old men of the four circuits; Xun overnight as a traveler in bonds suddenly stood above the multitude; meeting the generals he used courtyard ceremony for each; the Founder especially prized him.

units.zh: 未幾，表為鄜州留後。
units.en: Soon he was named acting commissioner of Fu.
units.literal: Before long he was memorialized acting commissioner of Fu prefecture.

units.zh: 是時，邠、岐之眾，屢寇其境，鄩禦捍備至，太祖以其地遠，慮失鄩，即令棄郡引軍屯於同州。
units.en: Bin and Qi raiders harried his frontier; he held them off, but the Founder, fearing to lose him so far away, pulled him back to Tong.
units.literal: At that time Bin and Qi raiders repeatedly harried the border; Xun defended with utmost care; the Founder, fearing to lose him in so distant a post, ordered the commandery abandoned and the army shifted to camp at Tong prefecture.

units.zh: 天祐二年二月，授右金吾衛大將軍，充街使。
units.en: In the second month of Tianyou 2 he became senior general of the Right Golden Guard and street commissioner.
units.literal: Tianyou year 2, second month, he was appointed senior general of the Right Golden Guard and street commissioner.

units.zh: 三年正月，太祖授元帥之任，以鄩為元帥府都押牙，執金吾如故。
units.en: In the first month of Tianyou 3 the Founder became commander-in-chief and made Xun his headquarters chief yamen officer while keeping the Golden Guard post.
units.literal: Tianyou year 3, first month, the Founder received the post of commander-in-chief and made Xun chief jailer of the commander's headquarters, retaining Golden Guard duties.

units.zh: 開平元年，授右金吾上將軍，充諸軍馬步都指揮使。
units.en: In Kaiping 1 he was made senior general of the Right Golden Guard and supreme horse-and-foot commander.
units.literal: Kaiping year 1, he was appointed senior general of the Right Golden Guard and overall commander of all armies' horse and foot.

units.zh: 其年秋，與諸將征潞州，遷檢校司徒。
units.en: That autumn he marched on Luzhou with the other generals and rose to acting Minister of Works.
units.literal: That autumn, with the generals he campaigned against Luzhou and was advanced to acting Minister of Works.

units.zh: 三年二月，轉右威衛上將軍，依前諸軍馬步都虞候。
units.en: In the second month of year 3 he was shifted to senior general of the Right Awesome Guard, continuing as overall horse-and-foot inspector of all armies.
units.literal: Year 3, second month, he was transferred to senior general of the Right Awesome Guard, continuing as overall horse-and-foot commander of all armies.

units.zh: 五月，改左龍武統軍，充侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使。
units.en: In the fifth month he became commander of the Left Dragon-Tiger army and of the palace guard horse and foot.
units.literal: Fifth month, he was changed to commander of the Left Dragon-Tiger army and commander of the palace guard's horse and foot.

units.zh: 其年夏，同州劉知俊反，引岐人襲據長安，分兵扼河、潼。
units.en: That summer Liu Zhijun of Tongzhou rebelled, led Qi troops in a surprise seizure of Chang'an, and posted men to hold the Yellow River and Tong Pass.
units.literal: That summer, Liu Zhijun of Tongzhou rebelled, led Qi men in a surprise seizure of Chang'an, and divided troops to hold the Yellow River and Tong Pass.

units.zh: 太祖幸陝，命鄩西討，即奮取潼關，擒知俊弟知浣以獻。
units.en: The Founder went to Shan and ordered Xun west; Xun at once seized Tong Pass and captured Zhijun's younger brother Zhihuan for presentation.
units.literal: The Founder went to Shan and ordered Xun to campaign west; he boldly seized Tong Pass and captured Zhijun's younger brother Zhi Huan for presentation.

units.zh: 遂引兵收復長安，知俊棄郡奔鳳翔。
units.en: He then recovered Chang'an; Zhijun abandoned the commandery and fled to Fengxiang.
units.literal: He then led troops to recover Chang'an; Zhijun abandoned the commandery and fled to Fengxiang.

units.zh: 太祖以鄩為佑國、同州軍兩使留後。
units.en: The Founder made Xun acting commissioner of both the Youguo and Tongzhou armies.
units.literal: The Founder made Xun acting commissioner of both Youguo and Tongzhou armies.

units.zh: 尋改佑國軍為永平軍，以鄩為節度使、檢校司徒，行大安尹、金州管內觀察使。
units.en: Soon the Youguo army was renamed Yongping army; Xun was made military commissioner, acting Minister of Education, acting Metropolitan Prefect of Da'an, and surveillance commissioner over Jinzhou.
units.literal: Soon Youguo army was changed to Yongping army, and Xun was made military commissioner, acting Minister of Education, acting Metropolitan Prefect of Da'an, and surveillance commissioner over Jinzhou.

units.zh: 是時，西鄙未寧，密邇寇境，鄩練兵撫眾，獨當一面。
units.en: The western frontier was still unsettled and lay close to the enemy; Xun drilled troops, steadied the men, and held the line alone.
units.literal: At that time the western frontier was not yet settled and closely bordered the enemy; Xun drilled troops and comforted the masses, holding one face alone.

units.zh: 四年，加檢校太保、同平章事。
units.en: In year 4 he was made acting Grand Guardian and co-rector of state.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was made acting Grand Guardian and Co-Rector of State.

units.zh: 庶人友珪篡位，加檢校太傅。
units.en: When Yougui the commoner usurped the throne, he was made acting Grand Tutor.
units.literal: When the commoner Yougui usurped the throne, he was made acting Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 乾化三年正月，丁內艱，友珪命起復視事。
units.en: In the first month of Qianhua 3 he mourned his mother; Yougui ordered him to resume office while in mourning.
units.literal: In the first month of the third year of Qianhua he mourned his mother; Yougui ordered him to resume office while in mourning.

units.zh: 未帝即位，尤深倚重。
units.en: When the Last Emperor acceded, he relied on him especially deeply.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor acceded, he relied on him especially deeply.

units.zh: 明年夏，詔鄩歸闕，授開封尹，遙領鎮南軍節度使。
units.en: The next summer an edict recalled Xun to court; he was made Prefect of Kaifeng and commissioner of Zhennan army in absentia.
units.literal: The next summer an edict summoned Xun to court; he was made Prefect of Kaifeng and commissioner of Zhennan army in absentia.

units.zh: 旋屬晉人寇河朔，鄩奉詔與魏節度使楊師厚禦之而退。
units.en: Soon the Jin raided Hebei; Xun by edict joined Wei commissioner Yang Shihou, repelled them, and withdrew.
units.literal: Soon thereafter the Jin raided Hebei; Xun received an edict and with Wei military commissioner Yang Shihou repelled them and withdrew.

units.zh: 九月，徐州節度使蔣殷據城叛。
units.en: In the ninth month Xuzhou commissioner Jiang Yin rebelled and held the city.
units.literal: Ninth month, Xuzhou military commissioner Jiang Yin held the city in rebellion.

units.zh: 時朝廷以福王友璋鎮徐方，殷不受代，末帝遣鄩與鄆帥牛存節率兵攻之。
units.en: The court had sent Prince of Fu Youzhang to Xu, but Yin refused to step down; the Last Emperor sent Xun and Yan commander Niu Cunjie against him.
units.literal: The court had posted Prince of Fu Youzhang at Xu; Yin would not yield; the Last Emperor sent Xun with Yan commander Niu Cunjie to attack.

units.zh: 殷求援於淮夷，偽吳楊溥遣大將朱瑾領眾赴援，鄩逆擊破之。
units.en: Yin called on the Huai; Yang Pu of Wu sent Zhu Jin to his aid; Xun routed the relief force.
units.literal: Yin sought aid from the Huai barbarians; false Wu ruler Yang Pu sent the great general Zhu Jin with troops to relieve him; Xun met and broke them.

units.zh: 貞明元年春，城陷，殷舉族自燔，於火中得其屍，梟首以獻，詔加檢校太尉。
units.en: In the spring of Zhenming 1 the city fell; Yin's family burned themselves; his body was recovered from the flames and his head presented; Xun was made acting Grand Commandant.
units.literal: Zhenming year 1, spring, the city fell; Yin and his clan burned themselves; his corpse was taken from the fire, the head sent up, and an edict advanced Xun to acting Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 三月，魏楊師厚卒，朝廷分相、魏為兩鎮，遣鄩率大軍屯南樂，以討王鎔為名。
units.en: In the third month Yang Shihou of Wei died; the court divided Xiang and Wei and posted Xun at Nanle with a large force, ostensibly against Wang Rong.
units.literal: Third month, Wei commander Yang Shihou died; the court split Xiang and Wei into two circuits and sent Xun with a great army to camp at Nanle, nominally to attack Wang Rong.

units.zh: 既而魏軍果亂，囚節度使賀德倫，送款於太原。
units.en: Wei troops soon mutinied, seized commissioner He Delun, and offered themselves to Taiyuan.
units.literal: Soon the Wei army did rebel, seized military commissioner He Delun, and sent submission to Taiyuan.

units.zh: 六月，晉王入魏州，鄩以精兵萬人自洹水移軍魏縣，晉王來覘，鄩設伏於河曲叢木間，俟晉王至，大噪而進，圍之數匝，殺獲甚眾，晉王僅以身免。
units.en: In the sixth month the Prince of Jin took Weizhou; Xun marched ten thousand picked men from Huan River to Wei county, ambushed the prince in riverside woods, surrounded him, inflicted heavy losses, and the prince barely escaped.
units.literal: Sixth month, the Prince of Jin entered Weizhou; Xun with ten thousand elite moved from Huan River to camp at Wei county; the Prince of Jin came to reconnoiter; Xun set ambush in the riverside thickets; when the prince arrived they shouted and advanced, surrounded him many times, killed and captured in great number, and the prince barely escaped with his life.

units.zh: 是月，鄩潛師由黃澤西趨太原，將行，慮為晉軍所追，乃結芻為人，縛旗於上，以驢負之，循堞而行，數日，晉人方覺。
units.en: That month he stole west toward Taiyuan; to cover his retreat he mounted straw dummies with flags on donkeys along the walls, and the Jin took days to notice the ruse.
units.literal: That month Xun secretly marched by Huangze west toward Taiyuan; before setting out, fearing Jin pursuit, he bound straw into human shapes, tied flags to them, loaded them on donkeys, and paraded them along the parapet; only after several days did the Jin realize.

units.zh: 軍至樂平，會霖雨積旬，師不克進，鄩即整眾而旋。
units.en: At Leping weeks of rain stalled the march; Xun withdrew in good order.
units.literal: When the army reached Leping, ten days of heavy rain blocked advance; Xun reformed the host and turned back.

units.zh: 魏之臨清，積粟之所，鄩引軍將據之，遇晉將周陽五自幽州率兵至，鄩乃取貝州，與晉軍遇於堂邑，鄩邀擊卻之，追北五十餘里，遂軍於莘縣。
units.en: He tried to seize grain-rich Linqing, met Zhou Yangwu from Youzhou, took Beizhou, fought the Jin at Tangyi, routed them, pursued fifty li, and camped at Shen.
units.literal: Linqing in Wei was a granary depot; Xun led troops to seize it, met Jin commander Zhou Yangwu coming from Youzhou, then took Beizhou, met Jin troops at Tangyi, met them with attack and drove them off, pursued the defeated more than fifty li, and encamped at Shen county.

units.zh: 增城壘，浚池隍，自莘及河，築甬道以通餉路。
units.en: He fortified Shen, dug moats, and built a covered road to the river for supplies.
units.literal: He heightened walls, deepened moats, and from Shen to the river built a covered way to keep supply lines open.

units.zh: 八月，末帝賜鄩詔曰：「閫外之事，全付將軍。
units.en: In the eighth month the Last Emperor wrote Xun: "All affairs beyond the camp gates I leave entirely to you.
units.literal: Eighth month, the Last Emperor bestowed an edict on Xun: "Matters beyond the passes I wholly entrust to the general.

units.zh: 河朔諸州，一旦淪沒，勞師弊旅，患難日滋，退保河壖，久無鬥志。
units.en: Hebei has collapsed, our troops are spent, disaster mounts daily, and we have lain idle on the Yellow River for want of heart to fight.
units.literal: The Hebei commands have in a day been lost; the army is worn, the troops exhausted, calamity grows daily; we have fallen back to guard the Yellow River bank and long lacked fighting spirit.

units.zh: 昨東面諸侯，奏章來上，皆言倉儲已竭，飛挽不充，於役之人，每遭擒擄，夙宵軫念，惕懼盈懷。
units.en: Eastern lords report empty granaries, broken supply lines, and constant captures—I brood on it day and night.
units.literal: Yesterday the eastern lords' memorials all came up, saying stores were gone, transport could not be filled, and men on campaign were taken captive again and again; I think of it night and day, fear filling my breast.

units.zh: 將軍與國同休，當思良畫，如聞寇敵兵數不多，宜設機權，以時翦撲，則予之負荷，無累先人。」
units.en: You share the dynasty's fate—find a way to strike while the enemy is few, and you will spare me disgrace before our ancestors."
units.literal: The general shares life and death with the state—think of a good plan; if the bandit enemy's numbers are not great, set stratagems and strike in season, then the burden on me will not shame our forebears."

units.zh: 鄩奏曰：「臣受國深恩，忝茲閫政，敢不枕戈假寐，罄節輸忠。
units.en: Xun replied: "I owe the throne everything and dare not sleep while holding the frontier.
units.literal: Xun memorialized: "Your servant has received deep grace from the state and disgraces this frontier post—how dare I not sleep on my spear and pour out loyalty to the last.

units.zh: 昨者，比欲西取太原，斷其歸路，然後東收鎮、冀，解彼連雞，止於旬時，再清河朔。
units.en: I meant to strike Taiyuan, cut their retreat, then recover Zhen and Ji and clear Hebei within weeks.
units.literal: Recently I wished to take Taiyuan in the west and cut off their return, then east to recover Zhen and Ji, break their linked wings, and in a matter of days clear Hebei again.

units.zh: 豈期天方稔亂，國難未平，才出師徒，積旬霖潦，資糧殫竭，軍士劄瘥，切慮蒼黃，乖於統攝，乃詢部伍，皆欲旋歸。
units.en: But the realm was still in chaos; no sooner had we marched than endless rain exhausted our stores, sickness spread, and the army wanted to turn back.
units.literal: Who expected Heaven still heaping chaos, the state's peril not yet ended—troops had barely marched when for ten days rain piled up, provisions were exhausted, and soldiers fell sick; I feared panic and loss of control, asked the ranks, and all wished to turn home.

units.zh: 凡次舍經行，每張犄角，又欲絕其餉道，且據臨清。
units.en: We camped in defensive arrays and tried to seize Linqing and starve them out.
units.literal: On every halt and march we spread horns; I also wished to cut their supply road and hold Linqing.

units.zh: 才及宗城，周陽五奄至，騎軍馳突，變化如神。
units.en: At Zong city Zhou Yangwu's cavalry struck like lightning.
units.literal: We had only reached Zong city when Zhou Yangwu suddenly arrived; his cavalry burst upon us, changing like spirits.

units.zh: 臣遂領大軍，保於莘縣。
units.en: I drew the main force back to Shen.
units.literal: Your servant then led the great army to hold Shen county.

units.zh: 深溝高壘，享士訓兵，日夜戒嚴，伺其進取。
units.en: There we dug in, fed and trained the men, and waited for their move.
units.literal: Deep moats, high ramparts, feasting the troops and drilling them, day and night on alert, watching for their advance.

units.zh: 偵視營壘，兵數極多。
units.en: Reconnaissance shows their numbers are vast.
units.literal: Spying on their camps, their troop numbers are extremely great.

units.zh: 樓煩之人，皆能騎射，最為敵，未可輕謀。
units.en: Their Loufan horsemen are deadly archers and must not be provoked lightly.
units.literal: The Loufan men can all ride and shoot and are the fiercest foemen—not to be lightly plotted against.

units.zh: 臣若苟得機宜，焉敢坐滋患難。
units.en: Had I seen a true opening, I would not have let disaster grow.
units.literal: If your servant could grasp the moment, how would I sit and heap calamity?

units.zh: 臣心體國，天鑒具明。」
units.en: My loyalty is before Heaven."
units.literal: My heart and body serve the state—Heaven sees clearly."

units.zh: 末帝又遣使問鄩決勝之策，鄩曰：「臣無奇術，但人給糧十斛，盡則破敵。」
units.en: Asked again for a winning plan, Xun said, "I have no trick—only ten hu of grain per man; when it is eaten, the enemy falls."
units.literal: The Last Emperor again sent envoys to ask Xun's plan for victory; Xun said: "Your servant has no wondrous art—only give each man ten hu of grain, and when it is gone the enemy will be broken."

units.zh: 末帝大怒，讓鄩曰：「將軍蓄米，將療饑耶？
units.en: The Last Emperor raged: "Are you stockpiling rice to feed yourself?
units.literal: The Last Emperor was greatly angered and reproached Xun: "General, are you hoarding grain to cure hunger?

units.zh: 將破賊耶？」
units.en: Or to beat the enemy?"
units.literal: Or to break the bandits?"

units.zh: 乃遣中使督戰。
units.en: He sent a palace envoy to force battle.
units.literal: He then sent a palace envoy to supervise the fighting.

units.zh: 鄩集諸校而謀曰：「主上深居宮禁，未曉兵機，與白麵兒共謀，終敗人事。
units.en: Xun told his officers, "The emperor knows nothing of war; courtiers will ruin us.
units.literal: Xun gathered the commanders and said: "The sovereign dwells deep in the palace and does not understand warfare; to plot with pale-faced fellows will in the end ruin affairs.

units.zh: 大將出征，君命有所不受，臨機製變，安可預謀。
units.en: A field commander may disobey orders and must adapt on the spot.
units.literal: When a great general goes forth, the ruler's command may be disobeyed; to seize the moment and change—how can that be planned beforehand?

units.zh: 今揣敵人，未可輕動，諸君更籌之。」
units.en: The enemy is not ready—think again."
units.literal: Now gauging the enemy, we must not move lightly—gentlemen, think again.

units.zh: 時諸將皆欲戰，鄩默然。
units.en: The officers wanted battle; Xun said nothing.
units.literal: Then all the generals wished to fight; Xun was silent.

units.zh: 他日，復召諸將列坐軍門，人具河水一器，因命飲之，眾未測其旨，或飲或辭。
units.en: Days later he lined the generals before the gate, gave each a cup of river water, and bade them drink; some drank, some would not.
units.literal: Another day he again summoned the generals to sit in a row before the camp gate, each with a vessel of river water, and ordered them to drink; the crowd did not fathom his intent; some drank, some refused.

units.zh: 鄩曰：「一器而難若是，滔滔河流，可勝既乎！」
units.en: Xun said, "If one cup is too much, how could you empty the Yellow River!"
units.literal: Xun said: "One vessel is hard like this—how could the rolling Yellow River ever be drained!"

units.zh: 眾皆失色。
units.en: All paled.
units.literal: All turned pale.

units.zh: 居數日，鄩率萬餘人薄鎮、定之營。
units.en: Days later he led ten thousand men against the Zhen and Ding camp.
units.literal: After several days Xun led more than ten thousand men to press the Zhen and Ding camps.

units.zh: 時鄩軍奄至，上下騰亂，殺獲甚眾。
units.en: The surprise threw them into chaos and cost them heavily.
units.literal: Xun's army came suddenly; above and below were in uproar; killed and captured were very many.

units.zh: 少頃，晉軍繼至，乃退。
units.en: Jin reinforcements arrived and he pulled back.
units.literal: Before long Jin troops followed and he withdrew.

units.zh: 二年三月，鄩自莘引軍襲魏州，與晉王戰於故元城，王師敗績，鄩脫身南奔，自黎陽濟河至滑州。
units.en: In the third month of year 2 he marched from Shen on Weizhou, lost to the Prince of Jin at old Yuancheng, fled south, and crossed from Liyang to Hua.
units.literal: Year 2, third month, Xun led troops from Shen to strike Weizhou, fought the Prince of Jin at old Yuancheng, the imperial army was badly defeated, Xun fled south, crossed from Liyang to Hua prefecture.

units.zh: 尋授滑州節度使，詔屯黎陽。
units.en: He was soon made commissioner of Hua and posted at Liyang.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed military commissioner of Hua and ordered to camp at Liyang.

units.zh: 三年二月，晉王悉眾來攻黎陽，鄩拒之而退。
units.en: In the second month of year 3 the Prince of Jin assaulted Liyang; Xun held him off and forced a retreat.
units.literal: Year 3, second month, the Prince of Jin brought all his hosts to attack Liyang; Xun resisted and made him withdraw.

units.zh: 及鄩歸闕，再授開封尹，領鎮南軍節度使。
units.en: Back at court he was again Prefect of Kaifeng and commissioner of Zhennan.
units.literal: When Xun returned to court he was again made Prefect of Kaifeng and military commissioner of the Zhennan army.

units.zh: 其年，河朔失守，朝廷歸咎於鄩，鄩亦不自安，上表避位。
units.en: When Hebei fell the court blamed him; uneasy, he asked to step down.
units.literal: That year Hebei was lost; the court blamed Xun; Xun too was ill at ease and memorialized to yield his post.

units.zh: 九月，落平章事，授亳州團練使。
units.en: In the ninth month he lost his chief-minister title and was sent to Bozhou as regimental commissioner.
units.literal: Ninth month, he was stripped of Grand Councilor rank and made regimental commissioner of Bozhou.

units.zh: 屬淮人寇蔡、潁、亳三郡，鄩奉命渡淮，至霍丘，大殲賊黨。
units.en: Huai raiders struck Cai, Ying, and Bo; he crossed the Huai, reached Huoqiu, and crushed them.
units.literal: When Huai raiders attacked Cai, Ying, and Bo, Xun received orders to cross the Huai, reached Huoqiu, and greatly destroyed the band.

units.zh: 五年，兗州節度使張萬進反，北結晉人為援，末帝遣鄩攻之，鄩為兗州安撫製置使。
units.en: In year 5 Yanzhou commissioner Zhang Wanjin rebelled and called on the Jin; the Last Emperor sent Xun against him as Yanzhou pacification commissioner.
units.literal: Year 5, Yanzhou military commissioner Zhang Wanjin rebelled, linked with the Jin in the north as aid; the Last Emperor sent Xun to attack; Xun was made pacification and disposition commissioner for Yanzhou.

units.zh: 是冬，萬進危蹙，小將邢師遇潛應王師，遂拔其城，梟萬進首以獻。
units.en: That winter, with Wanjin hard pressed, junior officer Xing Shiyu opened the gates to the imperial army; the city fell and Wanjin's head was sent in.
units.literal: That winter Wanjin was in desperate straits; junior officer Xing Shiyu secretly responded to the royal army; they then stormed the city and presented Wanjin's head.

units.zh: 十一月，製授泰寧軍節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事。
units.en: In the eleventh month he was formally made commissioner of the Taining army, honorary Grand Marshal, and Tongping Grand Councilor.
units.literal: Eleventh month, by formal appointment he was made Taining army military commissioner, honorary Grand Marshal, and Tongping Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 六年六月，授河東道招討使，與華州尹皓攻取同州。
units.en: In the sixth month of year 6 he was made Hedong campaign commissioner and, with Yin Hao of Huazhou, took Tongzhou.
units.literal: Year 6, sixth month, he was appointed Hedong campaign commissioner and with Huazhou's Yin Hao attacked and took Tong prefecture.

units.zh: 先是，河中朱友謙襲取同州，以其子令德為留後，表請旄鉞，末帝怒，命鄩討之。
units.en: Zhu Youqian of Hezhong had seized Tongzhou, installed his son Lingde as regent, and asked for a full commission; the Last Emperor ordered Xun against him.
units.literal: Earlier, Zhu Youqian of Hezhong had raided and taken Tong prefecture, made his son Lingde regent, and memorialized for the command seal; the Last Emperor was angry and ordered Xun to punish him.

units.zh: 其年九月，晉將李嗣昭率師來援，戰於城下，王師不利，敗兵走河南；
units.en: In the ninth month Li Sizhao of Jin came to relieve the city; the armies met below the walls; the imperial force was beaten and fled south of the river;
units.literal: That year, ninth month, Jin general Li Sizhao led troops to the relief; they fought below the walls; the royal army fared ill and the defeated troops fled south of the Yellow River;

units.zh: 橋梁陷，溺死者甚眾，鄩以餘眾退保華州羅文寨。
units.en: the bridge collapsed and many drowned; Xun drew the survivors back to Luowen stockade in Huazhou.
units.literal: the bridge gave way and very many drowned; Xun with the remnant withdrew to hold Luowen stockade in Huazhou.

units.zh: 先是，鄩與河中朱友謙為婚家，及王師西討，行次陝州，鄩遣使齎檄與友謙，諭以禍福大計，誘令歸國，友謙不從，如是停留月餘。
units.en: Xun was related by marriage to Zhu Youqian; on the western campaign he halted at Shanzhou and sent a proclamation urging Youqian to submit; Youqian refused, and Xun lingered there more than a month.
units.literal: Earlier, Xun and Zhu Youqian of Hezhong were marriage kin; when the royal army marched west he halted at Shan prefecture and sent an envoy bearing a proclamation to Youqian, explaining the great issue of fortune and ruin and urging return to the state; Youqian would not obey, and thus he lingered more than a month.

units.zh: 尹皓、段凝輩素忌鄩，遂構其罪，言鄩逗留養寇，俾俟援兵，末帝以為然。
units.en: Yin Hao, Duan Ning, and others who envied him accused Xun of stalling to let the enemy gather; the Last Emperor believed them.
units.literal: Yin Hao, Duan Ning, and their sort had long envied Xun; they therefore framed charges, saying Xun dallied and nourished the enemy to await relief troops; the Last Emperor believed it.

units.zh: 及兵敗，詔歸洛，河南尹張宗奭承朝廷密旨，逼令飲鴆而卒。
units.en: After the defeat he was recalled to Luoyang; Henan governor Zhang Zongshi, acting on a secret order, forced him to take poison.
units.literal: When the army was defeated, an edict recalled him to Luoyang; Henan governor Zhang Zongshi, carrying the court's secret order, forced him to drink poison and he died.

units.zh: 時年六十四，詔贈中書令。
units.en: He was sixty-four; an edict posthumously named him Palace Secretary.
units.literal: He was sixty-four; an edict posthumously made him Palace Secretary.

units.zh: 子遂凝、遂雍別有傳。
units.en: His sons Suining and Suiyong are treated in separate biographies.
units.literal: His sons Suining and Suiyong have separate biographies.

units.zh: 賀瑰，字光遠，濮陽人也。
units.en: He Gui, styled Guangyuan, came from Puyang.
units.literal: He Gui, styled Guangyuan, was a native of Puyang.

units.zh: 曾祖延，以瑰貴，贈左監門上將軍。
units.en: His great-grandfather Yan was posthumously made Left Gate senior general when Gui rose.
units.literal: Great-grandfather Yan, because of Gui's eminence, was posthumously made Left Gate senior general.

units.zh: 祖華，贈左散騎常侍。
units.en: His grandfather Hua was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant.
units.literal: Grandfather Hua was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant.

units.zh: 父仲元，贈刑部尚書。
units.en: His father Zhongyuan was posthumously made Minister of Justice.
units.literal: Father Zhongyuan was posthumously made Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 瑰少倜儻，負雄勇之志，遇世亂入軍。
units.en: In youth Gui was bold and high-spirited; when the realm fell into chaos he took to arms.
units.literal: Gui in youth was bold and free, with a fierce and brave will; when the age fell into chaos he entered the army.

units.zh: 朱瑄為濮州刺史兼鄆州馬步軍都指揮使，拔為小將。
units.en: Zhu Xuan, commissioner of Pu and commander of Yan's horse and foot, took him on as a junior officer.
units.literal: Zhu Xuan was Puzhou military commissioner and also Yanzhou horse-and-foot commander; he selected Gui as a junior officer.

units.zh: 唐光啟初，鄆州三軍推瑄為留後，以瑰為馬步軍都指揮使，表授檢校工部尚書。
units.en: In Guangqi of Tang the Yanzhou army made Xuan regent; Gui became horse-and-foot commander and was memorialized honorary Minister of Works.
units.literal: At Guangqi of Tang, Yanzhou's three armies pushed Xuan as regent; Gui was made horse-and-foot commander and memorialized honorary Minister of Works.

units.zh: 及瑄與太祖構隙，瑰受瑄命，數領軍於境上。
units.en: When Xuan quarreled with the Founder, Gui led repeated border raids at his orders.
units.literal: When Xuan and the Founder came into conflict, Gui received Xuan's orders and repeatedly led troops on the border.

units.zh: 乾寧二年十月，太祖親征兗、鄆。
units.en: In the tenth month of Qianning 2 the Founder marched in person against Yan and Yanzhou.
units.literal: Qianning year 2, tenth month, the Founder personally campaigned against Yan and Yan prefectures.

units.zh: 十一月，瑄遣瑰與太原將何懷寶率兵萬餘人以援朱瑾，師次待賓館，斷我糧運。
units.en: In the eleventh month Xuan sent Gui and He Huaibao of Taiyuan with ten thousand men to relieve Zhu Jin; they camped at the Guest House post and severed our supply line.
units.literal: Eleventh month, Xuan sent Gui with Taiyuan general He Huaibao to lead more than ten thousand men to relieve Zhu Jin; the army halted at the Guest House station and cut our grain route.

units.zh: 太祖偵知之，自中都引軍夜馳百餘里，遲明至钜野東，與瑰等接戰，兗人大敗。
units.en: The Founder learned of it, marched from Zhongdu through the night for more than a hundred li, and at dawn east of Juye met Gui and routed the Yan army.
units.literal: The Founder learned of it, led the army from Zhongdu by night for more than a hundred li, and at dawn reached east of Juye and joined battle with Gui and the rest; the Yan men were greatly defeated.

units.zh: 瑰竄於棘塚之上，大呼曰：「我是鄆州都將賀瑰，願就擒，幸勿傷也！」
units.en: Gui fled to a bramble mound and cried: "I am He Gui, commander of Yanzhou—I wish to surrender; spare me!"
units.literal: Gui fled to a bramble mound and shouted: "I am Yanzhou commander He Gui—I wish to surrender; please do not harm me!"

units.zh: 太祖聞之，馳騎至塚前，遂擒之。
units.en: The Founder galloped to the mound and took him.
units.literal: The Founder heard it, galloped to the mound, and there captured him.

units.zh: 並獲何懷寶及將吏數十人，徇於兗壁之下，悉命戮之，唯留瑰一人，釋縛，置之麾下；
units.en: He also took He Huaibao and dozens of officers, paraded them below the Yan walls, and had all but Gui executed; Gui was unbound and kept at headquarters;
units.literal: He also captured He Huaibao and several tens of officers and men, paraded them below the Yan ramparts, and ordered them all executed, keeping Gui alone; he loosed his bonds and placed him in his own command;

units.zh: 尋署為教練使，奏授檢校左僕射。
units.en: soon he was made drill instructor and memorialized honorary Left Vice Director.
units.literal: soon he was appointed drill instructor and memorialized honorary Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 瑰感太祖全宥之恩，私誓以身報國。
units.en: Grateful for the Founder's mercy, Gui privately vowed to repay the state with his life.
units.literal: Gui was moved by the Founder's grace in sparing him and privately vowed to repay the state with his body.

units.zh: 天復中，預平青州王師範，以功授曹州刺史兼先鋒都指揮使，加檢校司空。
units.en: In Tianfu he helped pacify Wang Shifan at Qingzhou, was made commissioner of Cao and vanguard commander, and given honorary Minister of Works.
units.literal: In Tianfu he took part in pacifying Qingzhou's Wang Shifan; for merit he was made Cao prefectural military commissioner and vanguard commander, and added honorary Minister of Works.

units.zh: 天祐二年，與楊師厚從太祖平荊、襄，授荊南兩使留後，未幾，征還，為行營左廂步軍都指揮使。
units.en: In Tianyou 2 he and Yang Shihou followed the Founder in pacifying Jing and Xiang, briefly held Jingnan as regent, then returned as left-wing foot commander of the field army.
units.literal: Tianyou year 2, with Yang Shihou he followed the Founder in pacifying Jing and Xiang, was appointed Jingnan dual-commissioner regent; before long he was recalled and made left wing foot-army commander of the field headquarters.

units.zh: 開平二年十月，授左龍虎軍馬步都指揮使。
units.en: In the tenth month of Kaiping 2 he was made Left Dragon-Tiger horse-and-foot commander.
units.literal: Kaiping year 2, tenth month, he was appointed Left Dragon-Tiger horse-and-foot commander.

units.zh: 十二月，改左衛上將軍，充六軍馬步都虞候。
units.en: In the twelfth month he became Left Guard senior general and inspector of the Six Armies horse and foot.
units.literal: Twelfth month, changed to Left Guard senior general and Six Armies horse-and-foot inspector.

units.zh: 三年五月，轉右龍虎統軍，未幾，加檢校司徒、邢州團練使。
units.en: In the fifth month of year 3 he was made Right Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief, then honorary Minister of Education and regimental commissioner of Xing.
units.literal: Year 3, fifth month, transferred to Right Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief; before long added honorary Minister of Education and Xingzhou regimental commissioner.

units.zh: 四年二月，改澤州刺史，充昭義軍節度留後、檢校太保，進封開國侯。
units.en: In the second month of year 4 he was made commissioner of Ze, regent of the Zhaoyi army, honorary Grand Guardian, and Marquis of the Opening State.
units.literal: Year 4, second month, changed to Ze prefectural military commissioner, regent of the Zhaoyi army and honorary Grand Guardian, advanced to Marquis of the Opening State.

units.zh: 乾化二年七月，授相州刺史，尋加檢校太傅。
units.en: In the seventh month of Qianhua 2 he was made commissioner of Xiang; soon he was also honorary Grand Tutor.
units.literal: Qianhua year 2, seventh month, he was appointed Xiang prefectural military commissioner; soon added honorary Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 有頃，轉左龍虎統軍。
units.en: Before long he was transferred to Left Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief.
units.literal: Before long he was transferred to Left Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief.

units.zh: 貞明二年，慶州叛，為李繼陟所據，瑰以本官充西面行營馬步軍都指揮使兼諸軍都虞候，與張筠破涇、鳳之眾三萬，下寧、衍二州。
units.en: In Zhenming 2 Qing prefecture rebelled under Li Jizhi; Gui, as western campaign horse-and-foot commander and army inspector, joined Zhang Yun in defeating thirty thousand men of Jing and Feng and taking Ning and Yan.
units.literal: Zhenming year 2, Qing prefecture rebelled and was held by Li Jizhi; Gui with his original rank was western campaign horse-and-foot commander and inspector of all armies; with Zhang Yun he broke thirty thousand men of Jing and Feng and took Ning and Yan prefectures.

units.zh: 三年秋，慶州平。
units.en: In the autumn of year 3 Qingzhou was pacified.
units.literal: Year 3, autumn, Qing prefecture was pacified.

units.zh: 十二月，瑰以功授滑州宣義軍節度使，依前檢校太傅，加同平章事，尋授北面行營招討使。
units.en: In the twelfth month he was made commissioner of the Xuanyi army at Hua, kept his honorary Grand Tutor title, made Tongping Grand Councilor, and soon northern campaign commissioner.
units.literal: Twelfth month, for merit Gui was made Xuanyi army military commissioner of Hua, still honorary Grand Tutor, added Tongping Grand Councilor, and soon appointed northern campaign commissioner.

units.zh: 四年春，晉人取楊劉城據之。
units.en: In the spring of year 4 the Jin seized Yangliu.
units.literal: Year 4, spring, Jin men took and held Yangliu city.

units.zh: 八月，瑰與許州節度使謝彥章領大軍營於濮州之行台村，對壘數月。
units.en: In the eighth month Gui and Xie Yanzhang of Xu encamped with a great army at the field headquarters village in Puzhou and faced the enemy for months.
units.literal: Eighth month, Gui with Xu prefectural military commissioner Xie Yanzhang led a great army and encamped at the field headquarters village in Puzhou, facing each other in opposing camps for several months.

units.zh: 一日，晉王以輕騎挑戰，瑰與彥章發伏兵奮擊，晉王僅以身免。
units.en: One day the Prince of Jin probed with light cavalry; Gui and Yanzhang sprang an ambush and nearly took him; he escaped only by a hair.
units.literal: One day the Prince of Jin challenged with light horse; Gui and Yanzhang loosed ambush troops and struck fiercely; the Prince of Jin barely escaped with his life.

units.zh: 先是，瑰與彥章不協，是歲冬十二月，復為諸軍都虞候朱珪所構，瑰乃伏甲士，殺彥章及濮州刺史孟審澄、別將侯溫裕等於軍，以謀叛聞。
units.en: Gui and Yanzhang had long been at odds; that winter Zhu Gui framed him again; Gui hid swordsmen and killed Yanzhang, Meng Shencheng of Puzhou, Hou Wenyü, and others, reporting a mutiny.
units.literal: Earlier Gui and Yanzhang were not in accord; that year, twelfth month of winter, army inspector Zhu Gui again framed him; Gui then hid armored men and killed Yanzhang, Puzhou military commissioner Meng Shencheng, deputy general Hou Wenyü, and others in the army, reporting it as a plot to rebel.

units.zh: 是月，瑰與晉人大戰於胡柳陂，晉人敗績，臨陣斬晉將周陽五。
units.en: That month at Huliu Slope Gui routed the Jin army and Zhou Yangwu was slain in the field.
units.literal: That month Gui fought a great battle with Jin men at Huliu Slope; the Jin were badly defeated and commander Zhou Yangwu was beheaded in the line.

units.zh: 既晡，瑰軍亦敗。
units.en: By dusk his own army too was beaten.
units.literal: When dusk came, Gui's army was also defeated.

units.zh: 五年春正月，晉人城德勝，夾河為柵。
units.en: In the first month of year 5 the Jin fortified Desheng and palisaded both banks.
units.literal: Year 5, first month, spring, Jin men walled Desheng and set palisades on both banks of the river.

units.zh: 四月，瑰率大軍攻其南柵，以艨艟戰艦扼其中流，晉人斷我艨艟，濟軍以援南柵，瑰退軍於行台，尋以疾卒，時年六十二。
units.en: In the fourth month Gui attacked the southern palisade with tower ships blocking the stream; the Jin cut the ships and crossed to relieve it; Gui fell back to the field camp and soon died of illness at sixty-two.
units.literal: Fourth month, Gui led a great army to attack their southern palisade, using tower ships to choke the midstream; Jin men cut our tower ships, crossed to relieve the southern palisade; Gui withdrew the army to the field headquarters and soon died of illness at age sixty-two.

units.zh: 詔贈侍中。
units.en: An edict posthumously made him Palace Attendant.
units.literal: An edict posthumously made him Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 長子光圖，仕後唐，為供奉官。
units.en: His eldest son Guangtu served Later Tang as a palace attendant.
units.literal: Eldest son Guangtu served Later Tang as a palace attendant.

units.zh: 康懷英，兗州人也。
units.en: Kang Huaiying came from Yanzhou.
units.literal: Kang Huaiying was a man of Yanzhou.

units.zh: 本名懷貞，避末帝御名，故改之。
units.en: His original name was Huaizhen; to avoid the Last Emperor's taboo name, it was changed.
units.literal: His original given name was Huaizhen; to avoid the taboo name of the Last Emperor, it was changed.

units.zh: 始以驍勇事朱瑾為列校。
units.en: For his fierce valor he first served Zhu Jin as a column commander.
units.literal: At first, for his fierce valor, he served Zhu Jin as a column commander.

units.zh: 唐乾寧四年春，太祖既平鄆，命葛從周乘勝急攻兗州。
units.en: In the spring of Tang Qianning 4, after the Founder took Yun, he ordered Ge Congzhou to press the victory and storm Yanzhou.
units.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Qianning of Tang, after the Founder had pacified Yun, he ordered Ge Congzhou to press the victory and attack Yanzhou in haste.

units.zh: 時朱瑾在豐沛間搜索糧餉，留懷英守其城。
units.en: Zhu Jin was foraging between Feng and Pei and left Huaiying to hold the city.
units.literal: At the time Zhu Jin was searching for grain and fodder between Feng and Pei, leaving Huaiying to hold the city.

units.zh: 及從周軍至，懷英聞鄆失守，乃出降。
units.en: When Congzhou arrived, Huaiying heard Yun had fallen and surrendered.
units.literal: When Congzhou's army arrived, Huaiying heard that Yun had fallen and came out to surrender.

units.zh: 太祖素聞其名，得之甚喜，尋署為軍校。
units.en: The Founder had long known his name and was delighted; he soon made him a military instructor.
units.literal: The Founder had long known his name and was greatly pleased to get him; he soon appointed him a military instructor.

units.zh: 光化元年秋，從氏叔琮伐襄、漢，懷英以一軍攻下鄧州。
units.en: In the autumn of Guanghua 1 he followed Shi Shucong against Xiang and Han and took Deng prefecture with one army.
units.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Guanghua, he followed Shi Shucong in campaigning against Xiang and Han; Huaiying with one army captured Deng prefecture.

units.zh: 三年，從征河朔，佐張存敬敗燕軍於易水之上。
units.en: In year 3 he campaigned in Hebei and helped Zhang Cunjing rout the Yan army above the Yishui.
units.literal: In the third year he followed campaigns in Hebei and assisted Zhang Cunjing in defeating the Yan army above the Yishui.

units.zh: 天復元年冬，太祖率師迎昭宗於鳳翔。
units.en: In the winter of Tianfu 1 the Founder led troops to welcome Emperor Zhaozong at Fengxiang.
units.literal: In the winter of the first year of Tianfu, the Founder led troops to welcome Emperor Zhaozong at Fengxiang.

units.zh: 時李茂貞遣大將符道昭領兵萬餘屯武功以拒，太祖命諸軍擊之，以懷英為前鋒，領眾先登，一鼓而大破之，擄甲士六千餘人，奪馬二千匹。
units.en: Li Maozhen sent Fu Daozhao with more than ten thousand men to hold Wugong; the Founder ordered an attack and made Huaiying vanguard. He led the charge, broke the enemy at one stroke, captured more than six thousand armored men, and seized two thousand horses.
units.literal: At the time Li Maozhen sent the great general Fu Daozhao with more than ten thousand troops to encamp at Wugong to resist; the Founder ordered the armies to strike; Huaiying was made vanguard, led the host up first, and in one drum broke them utterly, capturing more than six thousand armored men and seizing two thousand horses.

units.zh: 翌日，太祖方至，顧左右曰：「邑名武功，今首蕩逆黨，真武功也。」
units.en: The next day, when the Founder arrived, he told his attendants, "The place is called Wugong; today we first swept away rebels—truly martial merit indeed."
units.literal: The next day, when the Founder had just arrived, he looked to his attendants and said: "The district is named Wugong; today we first swept away rebels—truly Wugong indeed."

units.zh: 乃召懷英，大加獎激，仍以駿馬、珍器賜之。
units.en: He summoned Huaiying, praised him warmly, and gave him fine horses and precious vessels.
units.literal: He then summoned Huaiying, greatly commended and roused him, and furthermore bestowed fine horses and precious vessels on him.

units.zh: 二年四月，符道昭復領大軍屯於虢縣之漢穀。
units.en: In the fourth month of year 2 Fu Daozhao again encamped with a great army at Hangu in Guo county.
units.literal: Year 2, fourth month, Fu Daozhao again led a great army and encamped at Hangu in Guo county.

units.zh: 其建寨之所，前臨巨澗，後倚峻阜，險不可升，太祖遣懷英提騎數千急擊之。
units.en: His camp fronted a deep ravine and backed a steep height and could not be climbed; the Founder sent Huaiying with several thousand horse to strike at once.
units.literal: Where he built the stockade, in front was a great ravine and behind a steep height, impassably dangerous; the Founder sent Huaiying leading several thousand horse in haste to strike him.

units.zh: 道昭以懷英兵寡，有俯視之意，乃率甲士萬人，絕澗以挑戰。
units.en: Daozhao thought Huaiying too few to fear and led ten thousand armored men across the ravine to fight.
units.literal: Daozhao, seeing Huaiying's troops few, looked down on them; he therefore led ten thousand armored men, crossed the ravine to challenge.

units.zh: 懷英始以千騎夜鬥，戰酣，發伏以擊之，岐軍大敗。
units.en: Huaiying met him at night with a thousand horse, then sprang an ambush as the fight peaked; the Qi army was routed.
units.literal: Huaiying first fought with a thousand horse at night; when the battle grew hot he loosed ambush troops to strike; the Qi army was greatly defeated.

units.zh: 秋八月，鄜帥李周彝屯軍於三原，以援鳳翔；
units.en: In the eighth month Yan commissioner Li Zhouyi encamped at Sanyuan to relieve Fengxiang;
units.literal: Autumn, eighth month, Yan military commissioner Li Zhouyi encamped at Sanyuan to aid Fengxiang;

units.zh: 太祖命懷英討之，周彝拔軍而遁，追至梨園，因攻下翟州，擒其守來獻。
units.en: the Founder sent Huaiying against him; Zhouyi fled; the pursuers reached Liyuan, took Zhaizhou, and sent in the captured governor.
units.literal: the Founder ordered Huaiying to punish him; Zhouyi drew off the army and fled; they pursued to Liyuan, then attacked and took Zhai prefecture and captured its defender for presentation.

units.zh: 俄而岐軍屯奉天，太祖令懷英寨於岐軍之東北，以備敵人。
units.en: Soon Qi troops encamped at Fengtian; the Founder had Huaiying build a camp northeast of them to block the enemy.
units.literal: Before long Qi troops encamped at Fengtian; the Founder ordered Huaiying to stockade northeast of the Qi army to guard against the enemy.

units.zh: 一夕，岐軍大至，急攻其營。
units.en: One night a large Qi force stormed his camp.
units.literal: One night a great Qi army came and fiercely attacked his camp.

units.zh: 懷英以夜中不可驚動諸軍，獨以二千餘人抗數萬之眾，自乙夜至四鼓，身被十餘創，岐軍不勝而退。
units.en: Unwilling to rouse the whole army in the dark, Huaiying held the camp with two thousand against tens of thousands from the second watch to the fourth, took more than ten wounds, and beat the Qi force back.
units.literal: Huaiying, thinking the night unsuited to alarming the whole army, alone with more than two thousand men resisted tens of thousands; from the second watch to the fourth watch he received more than ten wounds; the Qi army could not win and withdrew.

units.zh: 昭宗還京，賜迎鑾毅勇功臣。
units.en: When Emperor Zhaozong returned to the capital, Huaiying was granted the title Meritorious Minister for Welcoming the Carriage, Bold and Brave.
units.literal: When Zhaozong returned to the capital, he was granted the title Meritorious Minister for Welcoming the Imperial Carriage, Bold and Brave.

units.zh: 是歲，淮人聞青、兗之叛，遣兵數萬以寇宿州。
units.en: That year, learning of revolt in Qing and Yan, the Huai sent tens of thousands to raid Suzhou.
units.literal: That year, Huai men, hearing of the rebellion in Qing and Yan, sent several tens of thousands of troops to raid Suzhou.

units.zh: 太祖命懷英馳騎以救之，淮人遁去，即以懷英為權知宿州刺史。
units.en: The Founder sent Huaiying at speed to relieve the city; the Huai fled, and he was made acting prefect of Suzhou.
units.literal: The Founder ordered Huaiying to gallop to the rescue; the Huai men fled; he was then made acting Suzhou military commissioner.

units.zh: 天祐三年冬，佐劉知俊破邠、鳳之眾五萬於美原，收五十餘寨，乘勝引軍攻下鄜州，以功授陝州節度使。
units.en: In the winter of Tianyou 3 he and Liu Zhijun routed fifty thousand men of Bin and Feng at Meiyuan, took more than fifty camps, followed up to Fu prefecture, and was made commissioner of Shaan.
units.literal: Tianyou year 3, winter, he assisted Liu Zhijun in defeating fifty thousand men of Bin and Feng at Meiyuan, took more than fifty stockades, pressed the victory to attack and take Yan prefecture, and for merit was appointed Shaan military commissioner.

units.zh: 太祖受禪，加檢校太保。
units.en: At the abdication he was made honorary Grand Guardian.
units.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, he was added honorary Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 開平元年夏，命將大軍以伐潞州。
units.en: In the summer of Kaiping 1 he was ordered to lead a great army against Luzhou.
units.literal: Kaiping year 1, summer, he was ordered to lead a great army to attack Luzhou.

units.zh: 將行，太祖謂懷英曰：「卿位居上將，勇冠三軍，向來破敵摧鋒，動無遺悔，至於高爵重祿，我亦無負於卿。
units.en: Before he marched the Founder told him: "You rank among my chief generals and your courage leads the host; in battle you have never failed, and I have not stinted rank or pay.
units.literal: As he was about to march, the Founder said to Huaiying: "You stand among the chief generals and your courage heads the three armies; in breaking the enemy and crushing their spears you have never left regret, and as to high rank and heavy salary, I too have not failed you.

units.zh: 夫忠臣事君，有死無二，韓信所謂『漢王載我以車，衣我以衣，食我以食，食人之祿，死人之憂』。
units.en: A loyal minister serves unto death—Han Xin said, "The King of Han gave me his carriage, his clothes, and his food; eating a lord's bread, one dies for his lord's troubles."
units.literal: A loyal minister serves his lord with death and no second thought—Han Xin said, 'The King of Han carried me in his carriage, clothed me with his robes, fed me from his table; eating a lord's salary, one dies for his lord's cares.'

units.zh: 我每思韓信此言，真忠烈丈夫耳！
units.en: I often recall Han Xin's words—truly a loyal and valiant man spoke them!
units.literal: I often think on Han Xin's words—truly the words of a loyal and heroic man!

units.zh: 如丁會受我待遇之恩，不謂不至，懷黃拖紫，裂土分茅，設令木石偶人，須感恩義，一朝反噬，倒戈授人，苟有天道明神，安能容此！
units.en: Consider Ding Hui: I favored him beyond measure—yellow seal, purple robe, lands and titles—yet overnight he turned traitor and joined the enemy; if Heaven and the spirits are just, how could that be borne!
units.literal: Take Ding Hui, who received my kindness—who could say it was not complete? Yellow seals and purple robes, fief and partition—set even a wooden or stone dummy and it must feel obligation; yet one morning he turned and bit the hand, gave his sword to the enemy—if Heaven has clear light and the spirits are bright, how could that be borne!

units.zh: 大凡孤恩負理，忠良不為。
units.en: To betray grace and violate right—no loyal man will do it.
units.literal: Generally, to betray grace and violate reason—loyal men will not do it.

units.zh: 我今掃境內委卿，卿當勉思竭盡。
units.en: I now entrust the whole campaign to you; strive with all your strength.
units.literal: I now entrust the realm within the borders to you; you must strive to exhaust yourself.

units.zh: 況晉人新得上黨，眾心未葉和，以十萬之師，一舉可克。
units.en: The Jin have only just taken Shangdang and their men are not yet settled; a hundred thousand troops should take it at once.
units.literal: Moreover the Jin have newly taken Shangdang; the hearts of the masses are not yet united; with a hundred thousand troops they can be taken at one stroke.

units.zh: 予當置酒高會，望卿歌舞凱旋。」
units.en: I shall hold a great feast and await your triumphal return."
units.literal: I shall set out wine at a high feast and look for your song and dance on triumphant return.

units.zh: 懷英惶恐而退。
units.en: Huaiying withdrew in alarm.
units.literal: Huaiying withdrew in fear and trembling.

units.zh: 六月，懷英領大軍至潞，率眾晝夜攻城，半月之間，機巧百變。
units.en: In the sixth month he reached Lu and assaulted the walls day and night; within half a month he tried a hundred stratagems.
units.literal: Sixth month, Huaiying led the great army to Lu and led the masses day and night in storming the city; within half a month his stratagems changed a hundred times.

units.zh: 懷英懼太祖之言，期於必取，乃築壘環城，浚鑿池塹，然而屢為晉將周德威騎軍所撓，懷英不敢即戰。
units.en: Mindful of the Founder's charge to take the city at all costs, he ringed it with camps and trenches, yet Zhou Dewei's cavalry harried him again and again and he dared not fight.
units.literal: Huaiying, fearing the Founder's words, aimed at certain capture, therefore built stockades ringing the city and dug moats and ditches; yet he was repeatedly harried by Jin general Zhou Dewei's horse and dared not give battle at once.

units.zh: 太祖乃以李思安代之，降為行營都虞候。
units.en: The Founder then replaced him with Li Si'an and made him field headquarters inspector.
units.literal: The Founder then replaced him with Li Si'an and demoted him to field headquarters inspector.

units.zh: 夏五月，晉王率蕃漢大軍攻下夾城，懷英逃歸，詣銀台門待罪，太祖宥之，改授右衛上將軍。
units.en: In the fifth month the Prince of Jin took Jiacheng; Huaiying fled home, presented himself for punishment at the Silver Terrace Gate, was pardoned, and made Right Guard senior general.
units.literal: Summer, fifth month, the Prince of Jin led a great army of tribal and Han troops and took Jiacheng; Huaiying fled back, went to the Silver Terrace Gate to await punishment; the Founder pardoned him and changed him to Right Guard senior general.

units.zh: 三年夏，命為侍衛諸軍都指揮使，尋出為陝州節度使兼西路行營副招討使。
units.en: In the summer of year 3 he commanded the Palace Guard horse and foot, then went out as commissioner of Shaan and deputy western campaign commissioner.
units.literal: Year 3, summer, he was ordered Palace Guard horse-and-foot commander; soon sent out as Shaan military commissioner and western campaign deputy commissioner.

units.zh: 及劉知俊奔鳳翔，引岐軍以圖靈武。
units.en: When Liu Zhijun fled to Fengxiang he led Qi troops against Lingwu.
units.literal: When Liu Zhijun fled to Fengxiang, he led Qi troops to aim at Lingwu.

units.zh: 太祖遣懷英率兵救之，師次長城嶺，為知俊邀擊，懷英敗歸。
units.en: The Founder sent Huaiying to relieve Lingwu; at Changcheng Ridge Zhijun intercepted him and he retreated defeated.
units.literal: The Founder sent Huaiying with troops to rescue; the army reached Changcheng Ridge, was intercepted by Zhijun, and Huaiying was defeated and returned.

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》云：還至升平，知俊掩擊之，懷英大敗。
units.en: (Ouyang's 《History of the Five Dynasties》 says that on the return to Shengping, Zhijun ambushed him and Huaiying was routed.
units.literal: (The 《History of the Five Dynasties》 by Ouyang says: Returning to Shengping, Zhijun ambushed him and Huaiying was greatly defeated.

units.zh: 據《通鑒》：懷貞等還，至三水，知俊遣兵據險邀之，左龍驤軍使壽張王彥章力戰，懷貞等乃得過。
units.en: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 records that on the retreat to Sanshui, Zhijun blocked the passes; Wang Yanzhang of Shouzhang, commander of the Left Dragon-Valiant army, fought hard and Huaiying got through.
units.literal: According to the 《Comprehensive Mirror》: Huaiying and the rest returned; reaching Sanshui, Zhijun sent troops to hold the defiles and intercept them; Left Dragon-Valiant army commander Wang Yanzhang of Shouzhang fought fiercely and Huaiying and the rest were then able to pass.

units.zh: 懷貞與裨將李德遇、許從實、王審權分道而行，皆與援兵不相值。
units.en: Huaiying, Li Deyu, Xu Congshi, and Wang Shenquan took separate routes and none met the relief column.
units.literal: Huaiying with deputy generals Li Deyu, Xu Congshi, and Wang Shenquan marched on separate routes and all failed to meet the relief troops.

units.zh: 至升平，劉知俊伏兵山口，懷貞大敗，僅以身免，德遇等軍皆沒。
units.en: At Shengping, Zhijun ambushed the pass; Huaiying was shattered and barely escaped; Deyu and the others were wiped out.
units.literal: Reaching Shengping, Liu Zhijun set ambush at the mountain pass; Huaiying was greatly defeated and barely escaped with his life; Deyu and the rest's armies were all lost.

units.zh: 蓋懷英過長城嶺之險已為邀擊，後又敗於升平也。）〉
units.en: Thus Huaiying was first intercepted at Changcheng Ridge and defeated again at Shengping.)〉
units.literal: So Huaiying had already been intercepted at the danger of Changcheng Ridge and afterward was again defeated at Shengping.)〉

units.zh: 四年春，移華州節度使。
units.en: In the spring of year 4 he was transferred to commissioner of Huazhou.
units.literal: Year 4, spring, he was transferred to Huazhou military commissioner.

units.zh: 乾化二年秋，命為河中行營都招討使，與晉軍戰於白徑嶺，敗歸於陝。
units.en: In the autumn of Qianhua 2 he was made Hezhong field commander-in-chief, fought the Jin at Baijing Ridge, was beaten, and withdrew to Shaan.
units.literal: Qianhua year 2, autumn, he was ordered Hezhong field headquarters commander-in-chief; he fought Jin troops at Baijing Ridge, was defeated, and returned to Shaan.

units.zh: 末帝嗣位，以岐軍屢犯秦、雍，命懷英為永平軍節度使、大安尹，累加官至中書令。
units.en: When the Last Emperor came to the throne, Qi raids on Qin and Yong led him to make Huaiying commissioner of the Yongping army and governor of Da'an, advancing in stages to Palace Secretary.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor succeeded, because Qi troops repeatedly raided Qin and Yong, he ordered Huaiying Yongping army military commissioner and Da'an governor, and in repeated steps advanced to Palace Secretary.

units.zh: 貞明中，卒於鎮。
units.en: He died in office during Zhenming.
units.literal: In Zhenming he died in his command.

units.zh: 王景仁，
units.en: Wang Jingren,
units.literal: Wang Jingren,

units.zh: 〈（景仁本名茂章，避梁諱改焉。
units.en: (Jingren was originally named Maozhang and changed his name to avoid the Liang taboo.
units.literal: (Jingren's original name was Maozhang; it was changed to avoid the Liang taboo.

units.zh: 詳見《通鑒注》。）〉
units.en: See the commentary to the 《Zizhi Tongjian》 for details.)〉
units.literal: See the 《Comprehensive Mirror》 commentary for details.)〉

units.zh: 廬州合淝人。
units.en: came from Hefei in Luzhou.
units.literal: a native of Hefei in Luzhou.

units.zh: 材質魁偉，性暴率，無威儀，善用槊，頗推驍悍。
units.en: Huge in frame and blunt in manner, without courtly bearing, he excelled with the spear and was famed for ferocity.
units.literal: His build was huge and imposing; his nature was violent and blunt, without dignified bearing; he was skilled with the spear and much esteemed for fierce valor.

units.zh: 在淮南累職為都指揮使，楊行密偽署宣州節度使。
units.en: In Huainan he rose to supreme commander; Yang Xingmi gave him the false title of commissioner of Xuanzhou.
units.literal: In Huainan he repeatedly served as commander-in-chief; Yang Xingmi falsely appointed him Xu prefectural military commissioner.

units.zh: 行密死，子渥自立，忌其勇悍，且有私憾，欲害之。
units.en: After Xingmi's death his son Wo seized power, feared Jingren's prowess, and, holding a private grudge, meant to kill him.
units.literal: When Xingmi died, his son Wo set himself up; he feared Jingren's fierce valor and, having a private grudge, wished to harm him.

units.zh: 景仁棄宛陵，以腹心百人歸吳越王錢鏐，鏐辟為兩府行軍司馬，具以狀聞。
units.en: Jingren fled Wannling with a hundred trusted followers to Qian Liu of Wuyue, who made him field marshal and reported the matter to court.
units.literal: Jingren abandoned Wannling and with a hundred trusted men went over to Wuyue King Qian Liu; Liu appointed him field headquarters marshal of both prefectures and reported the matter in full.

units.zh: 太祖復命遙領宣州節度使、檢校太傅、同平章事。
units.en: The Founder again gave him distant appointment as commissioner of Xuanzhou, honorary Grand Tutor, and Tongping Grand Councilor.
units.literal: The Founder again ordered him to hold Xu prefecture military commissioner at a distance, honorary Grand Tutor, and Tongping Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 鏐以淮寇終為巨患，欲速平之，命景仁奉表至闕，麵陳水陸之計，請合禁旅。
units.en: Qian Liu, seeing the Huai rebels as a lasting menace, wished a swift pacification; he sent Jingren to court with a memorial and a face-to-face plan for land and water forces, asking that imperial troops join the campaign.
units.literal: Liu, because Huai bandits would in the end be a great peril, wished to pacify them quickly; he ordered Jingren to present a memorial at court and explain his plan for land and water forces face to face, asking to combine with the forbidden troops.

units.zh: 太祖異禮待之，頒賜殊厚，顧曰：「待我平代北寇，當盡以王師付汝南討。」
units.en: The Founder honored him with unusual courtesy and rich gifts and said, "When I have pacified the northern raiders, I will give you the whole imperial army for the southern campaign."
units.literal: The Founder treated him with unusual courtesy and gave extraordinarily rich rewards, turning to say: "When I have pacified the northern frontier raiders, I will entrust all the royal army to you for the southern campaign."

units.zh: 於是留京師，每預丞相行列。
units.en: He stayed at the capital and regularly took his place among the chief ministers.
units.literal: He therefore remained at the capital and each time took his place in the chief ministers' ranks.

units.zh: 劉知俊之叛也，從駕至陝，始佐楊師厚西入關。
units.en: When Liu Zhijun rebelled, he followed the court to Shan and at first aided Yang Shihou in marching west through the pass.
units.literal: When Liu Zhijun rebelled, he followed the imperial carriage to Shan and at first aided Yang Shihou in entering the pass westward.

units.zh: 兵未交，知俊棄馮翊走，進克雍、華，降王建、張君練，頗預戰有功，太祖嘉之。
units.en: Before battle was joined Zhijun fled Fengyi; Jingren took Yong and Hua, won over Wang Jian and Zhang Junlian, fought with distinction, and won the Founder's praise.
units.literal: Before the armies clashed, Zhijun abandoned Fengyi and fled; he advanced to take Yong and Hua, received the surrender of Wang Jian and Zhang Junlian, took part in several battles with merit, and the Founder praised him.

units.zh: 時鎮、定作逆，朋附沙陀，遂擢為上將，付步騎十萬，為北面行營都招討使。
units.en: When Zhen and Ding rebelled with the Shatuo, he was made supreme commander with one hundred thousand troops and overall northern campaign commander.
units.literal: At that time Zhen and Ding rebelled, allying with the Shatuo; he was therefore promoted to supreme commander, given one hundred thousand foot and horse, and made overall northern campaign commander.

units.zh: 開平二年正月二日，與晉軍戰於柏鄉，王師敗績。
units.en: On the second day of the first month of Kaiping 2 he fought the Jin at Baixiang and the imperial army was routed.
units.literal: Kaiping year 2, first month, second day, he fought the Jin army at Baixiang; the royal army was badly defeated.

units.zh: 太祖怒甚，拘之私第。
units.en: The Founder was enraged and kept him under house arrest.
units.literal: The Founder was furious and detained him at his private residence.

units.zh: 然以兩浙元勳所薦，且欲收其後效，止落平章事、罷兵柄而已。
units.en: Yet because Wuyue's founding generals had recommended him and the Founder still hoped for service, he only lost his Grand Councilor title and command of troops.
units.literal: But because he was recommended by the founding meritorious men of the two Zhes, and wishing to gain his later effectiveness, only removed him as Grand Councilor and stripped military command—that was all.

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》：景仁及晉人戰，大敗於柏鄉。
units.en: (Ouyang's history says Jingren fought the Jin and was routed at Baixiang.
units.literal: (The 《History of the Five Dynasties》 says: Jingren fought the Jin and was greatly defeated at Baixiang.

units.zh: 景仁歸訴於太祖，太祖曰：「吾亦知之，蓋韓、李思安輕汝為客，而不從節度爾。」）〉
units.en: He returned and complained; the Founder said, "I know—it was because Han and Li Si'an treated you as an outsider and would not heed your orders.")〉
units.literal: Jingren returned and complained to the Founder; the Founder said: "I know it too—it was surely because Han and Li Si'an looked on you as a guest and would not obey your command.")〉

units.zh: 數月，復其官爵。
units.en: Several months later his titles were restored.
units.literal: Several months later, his office and rank were restored.

units.zh: 末帝即位，復用為南面北面行營招討應接使，以兵萬餘人伐壽州，至霍丘接戰，擒賊將袁叢、王彥威、王璠等送京師。
units.en: At the Last Emperor's accession he was again made liaison pacification commissioner for the southern and northern campaigns; with more than ten thousand men he attacked Shou, fought at Huoqiu, and sent the rebel generals Yuan Cong, Wang Yanwei, and Wang Fan to court.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, he was again employed as southern and northern campaign liaison pacification commissioner; with more than ten thousand troops he attacked Shouzhou; at Huoqiu they joined battle and captured the rebel generals Yuan Cong, Wang Yanwei, Wang Fan and others and sent them to the capital.

units.zh: 俄而朱瑾以大軍至，景仁力戰不屈，常以數騎身先奮擊，寇不敢逼，乃引兵還。
units.en: Zhu Jin soon came with a great host; Jingren fought on without yielding, often charging ahead with a few horsemen; the enemy dared not close, and he withdrew.
units.literal: Before long Zhu Jin came with a great army; Jingren fought stubbornly without yielding, often with several horsemen taking the lead in fierce charges; the bandits did not dare press him, and he then led the army back.

units.zh: 及濟淮，復為殿軍，故不甚衄，瑾亦不敢北渡。
units.en: Crossing the Huai on the return he covered the rear, so the army was not badly mauled; Zhu Jin also dared not pursue north of the river.
units.literal: When crossing the Huai on the return, he again served as rear guard, so they did not suffer great defeat; Zhu Jin also did not dare cross north of the Huai.

units.zh: 〈（《九國誌·朱景傳》：王茂章來寇，度淮水可涉處立表識之，景易置於深潭水中，立表浮木之上。
units.en: (When Wang Maozhang raided, he marked the Huai fords; Zhu Jing then moved the markers to deep water on floating logs.
units.literal: (When Wang Maozhang came to raid, he gauged where the Huai could be forded and set markers; Jing moved them to deep pools, setting the markers on floating logs.

units.zh: 茂軍敗，望表而涉，溺死者大半，積其屍為京觀。）〉
units.en: Maozhang's men followed the markers, drowned by the half, and their bodies were heaped into a trophy mound.)〉
units.literal: When Mao's army was defeated, they looked at the markers and crossed; more than half drowned; their corpses were piled into a barrow-display.)〉

units.zh: 及歸，病疽而卒。
units.en: After his return he died of a carbuncle.
units.literal: On returning, he fell ill with carbuncle and died.

units.zh: 詔贈太尉。
units.en: An edict posthumously made him Grand Marshal.
units.literal: An edict posthumously honored him as Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 史臣曰：劉鄩以機略自負，賀瑰以忠毅見稱，懷英以驍勇佐時，景仁以貞純許國，較其器業，皆名將也。
units.en: The historian writes: Liu Xun trusted his stratagem, He Gui was praised for loyalty, Kang Huaiying for fierce service, Wang Jingren for steadfast devotion—each in his way a famous commander.
units.literal: The historian writes: Liu Xun prided himself on stratagem, He Gui was famed for loyal resolve, Huaiying aided the age with fierce courage, Jingren pledged pure loyalty to the state; comparing their capacities, all were famous generals.

units.zh: 然雖有善戰之勞，亦有敗軍之咎，則知兵無常勝，豈虛言哉！
units.en: Yet each who fought well also knew defeat; arms win no permanent victory—that is no empty saying.
units.literal: Yet though each had merit in good fighting, each also had the fault of defeated armies—thus one knows arms have no constant victory; how could that be empty talk!

units.zh: 然鄩之據兗州，盡誠於師範，比跡於英公，方之數侯，加一等矣。
units.en: Yet in holding Yanzhou and serving Shifan with full loyalty, Liu Xun matched the Duke of Ying and stood a rank above these other lords.
units.literal: Yet in Liu Xun's holding of Yanzhou, his full loyalty to Shifan, his likeness to the Duke of Ying, compared with these several marquises, he ranks one degree higher.

units.zh: 六月，遣兗州節度使劉鄩、華州節度使尹皓、崇州節度使溫昭圖、莊宅使段凝領軍攻同州。
units.en: In the sixth month Liu Yan of Yan, Yin Hao of Hua, Wen Zhaotu of Chong, and Duan Ning of the Manor Estates marched on Tongzhou.
units.literal: In the sixth month, Yanzhou military commissioner Liu Yan, Huazhou military commissioner Yin Hao, Chongzhou military commissioner Wen Zhaotu, and Manor Estates commissioner Duan Ning led armies to attack Tongzhou.

units.zh: 八月，段凝、張朗攻衛州，下之，獲刺史李存儒以獻。
units.en: In the eighth month Duan Ning and Zhang Lang took Weizhou and sent captive commissioner Li Cunru to court.
units.literal: In the eighth month Duan Ning and Zhang Lang attacked Weizhou and took it, capturing military commissioner Li Cunru and presenting him.

units.zh: 己巳，王彥章、段凝圍楊劉城。
units.en: On jisi Wang Yanzhang and Duan Ning besieged Yangliu.
units.literal: On jisi, Wang Yanzhang and Duan Ning besieged Yangliu city.

units.zh: 八月，以段凝代王彥章為北面行營招討使。
units.en: In the eighth month Duan Ning replaced Wang Yanzhang as northern commander.
units.literal: In the eighth month Duan Ning replaced Wang Yanzhang as Northern Campaign Pacification commissioner.

units.zh: 戊子，段凝營於王村，引軍自高陵渡河，復臨河而還。
units.en: On wuzi Duan Ning camped at Wang village, crossed at Gaoling, and maneuvered along the river.
units.literal: On wuzi, Duan Ning encamped at Wang village, led troops from Gaoling to cross the river, and again faced the river returning.

units.zh: 帝聞中都之敗，唐軍長驅將至，遣張漢倫馳驛召段凝於河上；
units.en: Hearing of Zhongdu’s fall and Tang’s advance, the Emperor dispatched Zhang Hanlun to recall Duan Ning from the river;
units.literal: The Emperor heard of Zhongdu’s defeat and that Tang troops were coming at speed; he sent Zhang Hanlun by post relay to summon Duan Ning on the river;

units.zh: 時禁軍尚有四千人，朱圭請以拒唐軍，帝不從，登建國門召開封尹王瓚，謂之曰：「段凝未至，社稷係卿方略。」
units.en: Four thousand guards remained; Zhu Gui begged to fight; the Emperor refused, climbed the Founding Gate, called Wang Zan, and said: "Until Duan Ning comes the realm rests on you."
units.literal: At the time the Imperial Guard still had four thousand men; Zhu Gui asked to use them to resist Tang troops; the Emperor did not follow, ascended the Founding Gate, summoned Kaifeng Intendant Wang Zan, and said to him: "Duan Ning has not arrived—the altars depend on your strategy."

units.zh: 淮南楊溥遣使貢賀郊天禮物。
units.en: Yang Pu of Huainan sent envoys with gifts for the suburban rites.
units.literal: Yang Pu of Huainan sent envoys with tribute congratulating the suburban sacrifice.

units.zh: 進封河南尹兼河陽節度使張全義為魏王，兩浙節度使錢鏐進封吳越王。
units.en: Zhang Quanyi of Henan and Heyang was raised to Prince of Wei; Qian Liu of the two Zhes to King of Wu and Yue.
units.literal: Zhang Quanyi, Henan Prefect concurrently military governor of Heyang, was advanced and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei; Qian Liu, military governor of the two Zhe circuits, was advanced and enfeoffed as King of Wu and Yue.

units.zh: 五月，以唐朝宰臣張文蔚、楊涉並為門下侍郎、平章事；
units.en: In the fifth month former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;
units.literal: In the fifth month, former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;

units.zh: 壬午，保義軍節度使朱友謙進百官衣二百副。
units.en: On renwu Zhu Youqian of the Baoyi Army offered two hundred sets of court robes.
units.literal: On renwu, Zhu Youqian, military governor of the Baoyi Army, presented two hundred sets of official robes.

units.zh: 諸道節度使錢鏐、張宗奭、馬殷、王審知、劉隱各賜一子六品正員官，高季昌賜一子八品正員官，賀德倫賜一子九品正員官。
units.en: Commissioners Qian Liu, Zhang Zongshi, Ma Yin, Wang Shenzhi, and Liu Yin each received a regular sixth-rank post for a son; Gao Jichang an eighth-rank post; He Delun a ninth-rank post.
units.literal: Circuit commissioners Qian Liu, Zhang Zongshi, Ma Yin, Wang Shenzhi, and Liu Yin each had one son given a regular sixth-rank post; Gao Jichang one son eighth rank; He Delun one son ninth rank.

units.zh: 丙申，御元德殿，宴犒諸軍使劉捍、符道昭已下，賜物有差。〉
units.en: On bingshen he held court in the Hall of Primordial Virtue and feasted army commissioners from Liu Han and Fu Daozhao downward, with graded gifts.〉
units.literal: On bingshen the Emperor held court in the Hall of Primordial Virtue, feasted and rewarded army commissioners from Liu Han and Fu Daozhao down, bestowing goods in graded amounts.〉

units.zh: 太祖受禪，除右羽林統軍，尋佐劉鄩統兵收潼關，擒劉知浣獻之，乃以為右龍虎統軍兼侍衛指揮使。
units.en: At the Liang founding he was made Right Feathered Forest commander; he soon helped Liu Yan recover Tong Pass, captured Liu Zhihuan and presented him, and was then made Right Dragon-Tiger commander and commander of the palace guard.
units.literal: When the Founder received the mandate, Gui was made Right Feathered Forest commander; soon he aided Liu Yan in leading troops to recover Tong Pass, captured Liu Zhihuan and presented him, and was then made Right Dragon-Tiger commander and also commander of the palace guard.

units.zh: 其後破盧瑭、張至及朱瑄、朱瑾之眾，平定曹、濮，未嘗不在戰中。
units.en: He fought Lu Tang, Zhang Zhi, Zhu Xuan, and Zhu Jin, pacified Cao and Pu, and was never far from the fighting.
units.literal: Afterward he broke the hosts of Lu Tang, Zhang Zhi, Zhu Xuan, and Zhu Jin, pacified Cao and Pu—never absent from battle.

units.zh: 晉王遣都將李嗣昭、李存審、王建及率師來援同州，戰於城下。
units.en: The Prince of Jin sent Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji to relieve Tongzhou and battle was joined under the walls.
